rationale: Both are the same backtracking search. B has a docstring stating the contract and compares results with 'is not None' instead of relying on truthiness. Its recursive step chooses the matching orientation with if/elif and has a single shared return check, so there are no duplicated blocks. The elif is safe, because both halves can only match the open end when the stone is a double. A repeats the recurse-and-check block for each orientation, both in the helper and at the top level, which is noticeably more repetitive. B's top-level loop over an inline tuple of (first, end) pairs is a bit dense, and it tries both orientations even for doubles. Overall B is cleaner and better documented.
